title: Provenance and interpretation of annual, seasonal and demand-response experiment parameters

classification_definitions.prototype_inherited: A value read from or deliberately preserved from the declared DOE/PNNL reference building.
classification_definitions.literature_supported_scenario: A bounded experimental scenario within magnitudes or durations used in primary field studies or official research reports; it is not a universal standard.
classification_definitions.study_defined_sensitivity: A finite scenario grid declared by the study to test dependence on an assumption; it is not an externally prescribed value.
classification_definitions.data_derived_sensitivity: A perturbation estimated from the study observations and scaled through a declared sensitivity grid; it is not a measured longitudinal response of the same person.
classification_definitions.pre_control_selection_rule: A deterministic rule that selects dates from common reference loads before comparisons among controllers.
classification_definitions.accounting_horizon: The time window over which electricity use and subsequent recovery are measured.

doe_medium_office_2019.title: ANSI/ASHRAE/IES Standard 90.1-2019 Medium Office prototype
doe_medium_office_2019.supported_use: Reference-building geometry, HVAC system and occupied heating/cooling thermostat separation.
doe_medium_office_2019.not_supported_as: A human comfort or perceptual-temperature standard.

de_chalendar_2023.title: Unlocking demand response in commercial buildings: Empirical response of commercial buildings to daily cooling set point adjustments
de_chalendar_2023.supported_use: A 2 degree Fahrenheit (about 1.1 degree Celsius) cooling-setpoint increase was field-tested across 385 experiment-days in six commercial buildings.
de_chalendar_2023.not_supported_as: Proof that every building or climate will respond similarly, or that 1 degree Celsius is an optimal action.

lbl_commercial_dr_guide.title: Introduction to Commercial Building Control Strategies and Techniques for Demand Response
lbl_commercial_dr_guide.supported_use: Global temperature adjustment and pre-cooling followed by setpoint relaxation are established commercial-building demand-response strategies; rebound depends on the building, climate and schedule.
lbl_commercial_dr_guide.not_supported_as: A prescription of one event duration, preconditioning duration or temperature increment.

lbl_openadr_small_commercial.title: Open Automated Demand Response for Small Commercial Buildings
lbl_openadr_small_commercial.supported_use: Commercial field tests used two-hour events, setpoint adjustments of 2 to 4 degrees Fahrenheit, and pre-cooling periods of one to four hours; the report found one hour too short at the tested sites.
lbl_openadr_small_commercial.not_supported_as: A universal requirement for two hours of preconditioning or a transferable performance guarantee.

iea_ebc_annex_67.title: Characterization of Energy Flexibility in Buildings, IEA EBC Annex 67
iea_ebc_annex_67.supported_use: Flexibility characterization depends on initial state, user needs, climate and rebound or discharge after activation.
iea_ebc_annex_67.not_supported_as: A requirement that recovery must be measured for exactly 48 hours or that recovery is complete at 48 hours.

common_reference_anchor.basis: A single declared comparator is held outside the demand-guided controller candidate libraries. It supplies common service limits, fixed-tail identities and controller-independent event dates.
common_reference_anchor.interpretation: A reproducible common reference that makes service and event comparisons use the same anchor.

annual_probe_target_domain.basis: A declared computational domain around the inherited occupied thermostat levels, with dense probes around the main operating region. The personal-profile values themselves extend beyond this domain, so the range is not a claim about all human demand.
annual_probe_target_domain.interpretation: Controller optima and candidate comparisons are conditional on the simulated 20 to 27 degree Celsius target domain, with a 21 to 26 degree Celsius retained-candidate sensitivity audit.

annual_candidate_offsets.basis: A symmetric finite candidate library around each controller optimum. Field evidence supports temperature perturbations near 1 degree Celsius as operationally plausible, but does not make these five offsets an exhaustive or optimal library.
annual_candidate_offsets.interpretation: A bounded service-energy sensitivity over five predeclared offsets.

occupied_thermostat_deadband.basis: The experiment translates the midpoint of the official prototype occupied heating and cooling schedules while preserving their 3 degree Celsius separation.
occupied_thermostat_deadband.interpretation: An HVAC equipment-control deadband inherited from the fixed reference building.

dr_temperature_actions.basis: The tested increments are modest relative to published commercial-building field actions near 1.1 degrees Celsius and fall within the range of setpoint-reset experiments. The exact two-value grid remains a study choice.
dr_temperature_actions.interpretation: A bounded test of modest thermostat actions, not a search for each building's optimal action.

dr_preconditioning_and_event_duration.basis: Two-hour commercial events are documented, and commercial pre-cooling has been tested over one to several hours. The paired two-hour durations provide one representative scenario rather than a standard.
dr_preconditioning_and_event_duration.interpretation: Performance of the declared two-hour preconditioning and two-hour event protocol.

values.terminal_audit: final recovery hour plus available post-horizon hours

dr_recovery_horizon.basis: Flexibility accounting should include rebound and delayed energy. Forty-eight hours is a conservative declared window spanning two diurnal cycles, not a standard recovery time.
dr_recovery_horizon.interpretation: Net energy and service effects within the event and following 48 hours, supplemented by a threshold-free terminal-residual audit.

dr_event_service_limit_factors.basis: A predeclared relative sensitivity grid applied only during the two-hour event. Preconditioning and recovery retain the strict factor of 1.0.
dr_event_service_limit_factors.interpretation: Factor 1.0 is the strict common-service result; 1.05 to 1.20 show how event qualification changes under progressively relaxed modeled-service budgets.

fixed_tail_service_fraction.basis: A predeclared distributional endpoint tracks the tenth of profiles least served by the common reference, with membership fixed before comparing controls.
fixed_tail_service_fraction.interpretation: Performance for a fixed worst-served tenth under the declared reference.

dr_protected_zone_fraction.basis: A predeclared proof-of-concept allocation that withholds the event action from the 20 percent of zones ranked most vulnerable in the event direction.
dr_protected_zone_fraction.interpretation: One targeted-shedding scenario showing the consequence of protecting three of fifteen zones.

dr_minimum_preconditioning_deadband.basis: An engineering guard that prevents preconditioning commands from collapsing the translated dual-setpoint separation below 1 degree Celsius.
dr_minimum_preconditioning_deadband.interpretation: A conservative validity constraint for this action library.

seasonal_demand_shift.basis: Warm-minus-cool contrasts are estimated separately within place for the multinational and China observation sources. Symmetric plus/minus half-shifts preserve the annual midpoint while making the summer-to-winter separation equal to the estimated contrast at fraction 1.0; fraction 0.5 is a smaller sensitivity case.
seasonal_demand_shift.interpretation: A source-level sensitivity to observed warm-versus-cool demand contrasts across an annual simulation.

layouts: demand ordered in native zone order
demand ordered in reverse zone order
demand ordered with a five-zone cyclic shift

spatial_layouts_and_command_permissions.basis: The layouts keep the same 267 demand profiles and zone-slot counts while changing who shares a zone. The permission levels retain the same building and distinguish one building command, three floor commands and fifteen occupied-zone commands.
spatial_layouts_and_command_permissions.interpretation: Controlled mechanism tests that separate spatial grouping from the ability to issue independent commands.

values.selection_reference: qualified common 25 degree Celsius reference trajectory
selection_constraints: event contained within one local day
non-overlap of preconditioning, event and recovery windows

dr_event_date_selection.basis: A deterministic pre-control rule samples typical and high-load occupied conditions in every meteorological season. Published flexibility work shows strong dependence on weather, initial state and repeated operating conditions, but does not prescribe these exact quantiles.
dr_event_date_selection.interpretation: A balanced seasonal protocol that avoids selecting dates separately for each controller and brackets median and high-load conditions.

target_domain_contact.scope: Offset-zero commands only; 54 logical commands per controller and 15 occupied zones per command.
target_domain_contact.interpretation: Boundary contact occurs in both demand-guided controllers.

profile_centre_coverage.interpretation: The 20–27 °C operational search domain covers part of the reconstructed demand-center distribution.

event_date_protocol.interpretation: The realized protocol matches the predeclared balanced seasonal selection rule. It supports conditional event comparisons, not annual event-availability probabilities.

seasonal_contrast.interpretation: Contrasts are estimated within place and kept source-specific. They parameterize a sensitivity construction; they are not longitudinal changes observed in the same people.
